newsitem.title: UK: UK's National Grid to shed 750 jobs -paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's National Grid to shed 750 jobs -paper.

text.p: Britain's electricity transmission network National Grid Group Plc will this week reveal plans to shed some 750 jobs in an effort to save 1.0 billion stg over four years, the Observer said on Sunday.
"The job cuts, which represent almost one in five of the company's 4,000 workforce, are 50 percent greater than it had already announced," the weekly said.
"The company is likely to blame the cuts on its need to meet stringent price controls imposed by electricity regulator Offer."
Offer's director general, Stephen Littlechild, proposed stringent price cuts which will carve about four pounds from the annual average electricity bill, the paper said.
But they will also reduce National Grid's revenue by 20 percent in the year to April 1998 and by a further 4.0 percent below the rate of inflation in the next three years.
National Grid accepted them rather than seek a reference to the Monopolies and Merger Commission, the paper said.
The job losses will come on top of some 2,500 jobs the grid has axed since it was floated last year. --London Newsroom +44 171 52 7717
